turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I do not in the least comprehend you. Mr. Wickham’s situation, his conduct, and his feelings are all open to me. He has chosen to reveal everything. Your actions have been most deplorable.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I have been most unhappy since my arrival here, but I hope that I shall now begin to be at peace. I am no longer the man to seek the company and the confidence of Mr. Wickham.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am surprised at your manner, Mr. Darcy. Your past actions speak louder than any words you can now offer.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am aware of the weight of my past actions, Miss Bennet, and I seek to amend them as much as I can.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your actions have been a source of pain to many, Mr. Darcy, and it is not easily forgiven or forgotten.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am acutely aware of the pain I have caused, Miss Bennet. It is a burden I carry with me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your words may be sincere, Mr. Darcy, but your actions have spoken too loudly to be quickly silenced.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, I understand your distrust, and I do not expect it to be easily dispelled. My actions have been the cause, and I must live with the consequences.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I cannot pretend that your confession alters my opinion of you, Mr. Darcy. Your character has been a source of disappointment to me.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your opinion of me, Miss Bennet, is of the utmost importance to me. I will not defend myself against your just reproaches.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I am sorry to say that your past behavior has made it impossible for me to consider you in the light you now seek.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, it is true that my pride has been my greatest obstacle. I will endeavor to prove to you that my feelings for you are genuine and lasting.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your efforts will be in vain if they are motivated by a desire to change my opinion rather than a sincere wish to amend your character.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, I must admit that I have often acted against the dictates of my conscience, but I swear that my intentions for you are now solely to win your esteem and affection.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your words may be sincere, but your actions have spoken louder and left a deep impression. I cannot so quickly overlook the pain you've caused.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, your words cut deep, for they are a reflection of my own self-discovery. I will not rest until I have earned your forgiveness and respect.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your journey of self-reflection is commendable, but it must be accompanied by actions that match your words.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, I understand the gravity of your expectations and the weight of your judgment. My actions will indeed be my testimony, more so than my words.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, I appreciate your earnestness, but it will take more than promises to change my opinion. Show me that you have truly reformed.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Miss Bennet, your wisdom and insight are not lost on me. I shall endeavor to prove myself worthy of your esteem through deeds that reflect my inner transformation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: His misfortunes! yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
